campaign: Third predeclared external observational channel after Planck, ACT primary CMB, and SPT-3G primary CMB. This test targets the integrated gravitational-potential history through CMB lensing rather than another TT/TE/EE primary-CMB replication.

likelihood_mode.reason: Use the official ACT-only baseline lensing power-spectrum likelihood as a standalone lensing test, exactly as recommended by the likelihood documentation when not combining with primary CMB data.

observable.conversion: CLASS C_L^{phi phi} is converted to convergence using C_L^{kappa kappa} = [L(L+1)]^2 C_L^{phi phi}/4.
observable.multipole_policy: Use the native ACT DR6 act_baseline lensing multipole selection from the official likelihood. Do not post-select lensing multipoles after seeing eta.

inference.method: deterministic iterated local spectral linearization with bounded optimization, matching the frozen-model Planck/ACT/SPT campaign philosophy
inference.flat_or_weak_directions: Standalone lensing may weakly constrain some primary-CMB parameters, especially tau_reio. Keep the same six-parameter definition and bounded optimizer rather than adding post hoc external priors solely to improve eta sensitivity.

theory_support.reason: Provide sufficient lensing-theory support for the official ACT DR6 baseline likelihood. This is a technical theory-support choice made before reading eta.

report_regardless_of_outcome: official ACT likelihood variant and mode
any technical failures or pre-result amendments
anti_tuning: No change to KB, tauH0, p, lambda, CLASS patch chain, eta bounds, official ACT lensing variant, lens_only setting, or native lensing multipole selection may be motivated by the observed ACT lensing eta preference. Any required technical compatibility amendment must be committed before re-reading the eta result and may not alter the physical model.
interpretation: A positive lensing preference compatible in sign and scale with the Planck memory direction would be independent cross-observable support. A null or opposite-sign lensing result must be retained and reported without retuning.
